codeReview.summary: The feature adds offline perf-baseline tooling and committed fixture data as intended, but the regression gate does not actually lock the full fixture/schema contract, so the baseline check can miss contract drift.

issues.description: `eval:perf:check` only compares `fixture.sourceFiles` plus selected `metrics.*` fields. It never validates `schemaVersion`, `fixture.name`, `fixture.searchQuery`, or `fixture.aiSearchQuery`, and `readEvalPerfBaseline()` later accepts the baseline via an unchecked JSON cast. That means the command can still pass after fixture/query/schema drift, which violates the requirement that this tooling guard a fixed fixture dataset and schema-stable JSON output.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission AGENTS file's authoritative command list is stale after this feature: it does not mention the new perf baseline commands even though they are now part of the validation surface.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Mission AGENTS.md:18-22 lists only check/test/ci/smoke commands, while /root/projects/nya2/.factory/services.yaml defines `eval_perf: bun run eval:perf` and `eval_perf_check: bun run eval:perf:check`.

summary: Reviewed the feature handoff, commit 044fcfd, transcript skeleton, ops-worker skill, and changed files. The implementation is offline and mostly aligned with VAL-OPS-020, but review fails because check mode does not enforce fixture identity/schema stability, so it can miss contract drift that should invalidate the baseline.
